newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The People's Initiative for Reform, Modernisation and Action says it will file at least five million signatures with the Commission on Elections (Comelec) later this week, hoping Comelec will ask the Supreme Court to allow it to verify the signatures paving the way for a possible referendum for a Charter change. (MANILA TIMES)
- Autonomous Region in Moslem Mindanao Governor Nur Misuari says he can tap former Moslem rebels to neutralise kidnappers in the southern Mindanao island. (PHILIPINE STAR)

- Opposition senators vow to block the passage of an enabling law on people's initiative to amend the Constitution as they voice alarm over what they perceive as fresh efforts to stop the 1998 elections. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- President Fidel Ramos embarks on a nine-day working visit to the United Kingdom and Oman and a three-day state visit to Greece. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- The government has committed the opening of the domestic rice market from year 2005 to 2010 but refuses to peg the tariff rate at which rice can be imported. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- Creditor banks of the beleagurered Victorias Milling Corp say its bad debt of 6.5 billion peso may be understated by 200 million to 300 million pesos. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- The country's ship repair and building industry is facing stiff competition from other Asian shipyards which offer lower labour costs, Keppel Phils Holdings president Hoe Eng Hock says. (MANILA TIMES)
